title: Pause the Teen Argument and Agree When to Return | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: A disagreement with your teenager keeps circling. Both voices are getting louder, but neither person feels understood. Trying to win the argument right now can leave less room to solve the actual problem. Pause the discussion when emotions are high. A break should lead back to a conversation, not become days of silence. Try: I want to hear you, and I need to calm down. Can we come back to this after dinner? Choose a time you can keep. When you return, listen to their point of view and discuss one concern at a time. Keep necessary safety limits clear while working on the relationship.
